description: Logarithms are the inverse operations of exponents. They are primarily used to simplify complex mathematical calculations.

sections.title: Introduction to Logarithms
sections.description: A logarithm answers the question: to what power must a specific base be raised to yield a given number (argument)?

key_concepts.explanation: Here 'a' is the base, 'x' is the exponent, and 'N' is the argument. The base must always be a positive number and cannot be equal to 1.

sections.title: Fundamental Properties
sections.description: Logarithms follow several critical rules that make multiplying, dividing, and exponentiating numbers much easier.

sections.title: Base Change and Special Logs
sections.description: The base change theorem is utilized to alter the base of a logarithm during complex calculations.

key_concepts.explanation: When the base is 10, it is called a Common Logarithm and is often written simply as 'log'. When the base is 'e' (Euler's number), it is called a Natural Logarithm and is written as 'ln'.

sections.title: Solving Logarithmic Equations
sections.description: A systematic approach to finding the value of an unknown variable within logarithmic equations.

steps.title: Simplify the Equation
steps.detail: Use the fundamental properties of logarithms to combine multiple logarithmic terms into a single logarithm.

steps.title: Convert to Exponential Form
steps.detail: Rewrite the simplified equation from log_a(x) = y into its exponential form a^y = x to eliminate the logarithm.

steps.title: Verify the Solution
steps.detail: Substitute the obtained value back into the original equation to ensure the argument remains positive. Discard any extraneous solutions.

sections.title: Logarithmic Inequalities
sections.description: When dealing with inequalities (<, >, <=, >=) involving logarithms, the value of the base dictates the behavior of the inequality sign.

results: If log_a(x) > log_a(y), then x > y (The inequality sign remains unchanged).
If log_a(x) > log_a(y), then x < y (The inequality sign reverses).
